correctness.rationale: Every section [v,1] in the point-block incidence poset consists of its bottom, |N(v)| coatoms, and a new top; its pseudocomplements exist iff the local degree <=2 (chains or Boolean diamond). A point of degree >=3 has a coatom with no greatest disjoint companion. For admissible sections, only incomparable distinct points can have two minimal common upper bounds, and degree<=2 forces equal two-block neighborhoods. In the diamond the two coatoms pseudocomplement to one another, giving exactly t_bc(t_bc-1) ordered nonsingleton entries. A loopless multigraph of maximum degree 2 has double-edge components as the only identical two-edge-neighborhood point pairs. The labelled exponential component formula counts isolated points, paths, ordinary cycles and double edges, giving EGF (1-z)^(-1/2) exp(z/(2(1-z))+(2t-1)z²/4). Monotonicity/shift ratios for its positive coefficients and factorial-moment inversion rigorously imply Poisson(1/2), not simply numerical convergence. Independently recomputed exact full distributions of D for vertex sizes 2..8, including n=5 {0:253,1:80,2:15} and n=8 {0:152219,1:52024,2:8610,3:840,4:105}, matching coefficients.
